status: Task COMPLETE and VERIFIED: Release binary fixed (exit 0 both direct and valgrind). Debug binary also working (exit 0). Both pass valgrind with 0 errors, 0 definitely lost bytes. Solution: user_init() forces stdlib static object initialization before custom heap activation, preventing SIGSEGV during cleanup phase.

knowledge.content: Task: Fix crash in /app/ program that occurs in RELEASE mode but not DEBUG mode. Only /app/user.cpp can be modified.
Two libstdc++ versions: Debug at /usr/local/gcc-custom-debug/ (no optimizations), Release at /usr/local/gcc-custom-release/ (with optimizations). Custom in-house compiler source at /build/
Constraint: No memory leaks allowed (must pass Valgrind)

main.cpp implements custom global new/delete operators using CustomHeapManager. Global pointer g_custom_heap controls allocation routing. When non-null, allocations go to custom heap; when null, fall back to malloc.

Application class flow: constructor (empty) -> init() creates CustomHeapManager via placement new -> run() calls user_main() and does Monte Carlo -> destructor calls shutdown() which manually destroys CustomHeapManager and frees its memory.
CustomHeapManager allocates 10MB heap, uses bump allocator (heap_offset), deallocate() is no-op. Destructor memsets heap to 0xEF before freeing.

Solution implemented: user_init() in user.cpp forces stdlib static object initialization (std::cout, std::random_device, std::mt19937, std::uniform_real_distribution, std::string, std::stringstream, std::vector, std::setprecision, std::sort) before custom heap activates. This ensures these objects use regular malloc and can safely destruct after heap cleanup.

procedural.content: Step 4: Both debug and release versions compiled without errors using their respective libstdc++ versions and compile flags.

Step 5: Executed both binaries. Debug version runs successfully (exit code 0). Release version COMPLETES all output successfully but crashes with exit code -11 (SIGSEGV) AFTER printing "Computation completed successfully". This indicates the crash occurs during cleanup/destruction phase, not during main execution.

Step 6: Ran valgrind on release binary. Unexpectedly, valgrind completes with exit code 0 (no crash). The SIGSEGV only occurs when running ./release directly, not under valgrind instrumentation. This suggests the crash is related to optimization-specific behavior (timing, register allocation, or undefined behavior exposed by -O2) that changes under valgrind's memory checking.

Step 11-12 SUCCESS: Fixed release-mode crash by implementing user_init() in user.cpp to force initialization of stdlib static objects (iostream, random, string, stringstream, vector, iomanip, algorithm) BEFORE custom heap activation at main.cpp line 149. This ensures these objects are allocated via regular malloc rather than custom heap. When they destruct after main() returns, they don't crash trying to free custom heap memory. Release binary now exits cleanly with code 0 instead of SIGSEGV (-11).
